FIELD REFERENCE

Giant trevally (GT, ulua): size, names and trip planning

Giant trevally (Caranx ignobilis), often called GT, is a large Indo-Pacific reef predator. In Hawaii, its name is ulua aukea. The University of Hawaii gives an upper size of 170 cm and 80 kg. Those are species maxima, not the size to expect on a fishing trip.

Check Hawaii fishing licences, compare trevally name records, then explore reef and bottom trips.

Updated 2026-11-26 · Castward

IdentificationSteep head profile; dark mark at pectoral-fin base — Maui Ocean Center

Is ulua the same fish as giant trevally?

Ulua aukea identifies giant trevally in the University of Hawaii study. Use the full local name and Caranx ignobilis when you compare destinations. A short label on a trip listing can leave the target unclear. Ask which species the trip targets before you choose tackle or compare itineraries.

Read the source

How do you recognise a giant trevally?

Maui Ocean Center describes a steep head profile and a dark mark at the base of the pectoral fin. Courting males can look black, while females are silver. Use several features together when comparing trevally species; colour alone is a poor basis for identifying a fish before applying catch rules.

Read the source

How big can giant trevally get?

The University of Hawaii lists an upper size of 170 cm total length and 80 kg. Treat that as a biological size reference. Ask for the tackle requirements for your particular trip instead.

Read the source

What should you check before a GT fishing trip?

Start with the exact island, reef area and departure point. Then ask about boat or shore access, included tackle, the return time and the cancellation terms. Check that place’s licence and protected-area rules separately. A species range shows where a fish occurs; it does not establish permission to fish.

Read the source

What should you know about giant trevally?

What does GT mean in fishing?

GT is the common angler abbreviation for giant trevally.

What is the scientific name?

Caranx ignobilis.

What is its Hawaiian name?

Ulua aukea is the name used by the University of Hawaii.

Is every GT a large fish?

No. A maximum size does not describe every individual or an expected catch.

Do giant trevally live in groups?

Maui Ocean Center describes both solitary fish and schools.
